newsitem.title: UK: U.S. Carlson group to acquire British resort firm.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Carlson group to acquire British resort firm.

text.p: Carlson Companies Inc., which operates Radisson has agreed to acquire British package vacation company Inspirations Plc for 42 million pounds ($70.4 million), Carlson said Thursday.

Carlson, which operates Radisson hotels and T.G.I. Friday's restaurants, said the move underlined its commitment to international growth. Carlson is a privately owned group of companies based in Minneapolis.

The agreed offer values Inspirations' ordinary shares at 75p ($1.26), a premium of 22 percent to their closing price on Wednesday. News of the sale pushed shares up 10 pence ($1.68) to 71.5p ($1.20) by 1130 GMT on Thursday.

Carlson has agreed to buy the Inspirations convertible shares held by British Airways Plc for 5.5 million pounds ($9.2 million). It said the offer had the support of shareholders who control 63 percent of ordinary stock and 44 percent of the convertible share capital.
"The acquisition of Inspirations significantly improves our competitive position in the UK," said Michael Batt, chairman of CLG (UK), Carlson's British arm.
"It secures a supply of quality package tours for our customers and the improved efficiencies will enable us to offer those customers better value and choice than ever before," he added.

Carlson and Inspirations were already linked through the AT Mays chain of high street travel agencies. Inspirations owns 97 of the 400-strong chain while Carlson owned the rest and managed the whole chain.
Batt told Reuters the enlarged company planned to increase the number of retail outlets and re-brand them.
British competition authorities are in the process of probing vertically integrated travel agencies supplying what is a seven billion pound ($11.7 billion) market.
Thomson, the largest British tour operator, owns the Lunn Poly travel agencies while Airtours, its biggest competitor, has the Going Places chain.
Batt, who will chair the enlarged company, said the deal should increase competition.
